condition.i6_prior_conflict_resistance.description: Single-file Kotlin program required to implement a reversible counterfactual keyword remapping for a 3-operation arithmetic mini-language: source keyword 'add' really means multiply, 'sub' really means add, 'mul' really means subtract. Familiar lexical priors (add=addition, sub=subtraction, mul=multiplication) directly conflict with the supplied specification; model must follow spec over prior.
condition.i6_prior_conflict_resistance.raw_score_basis: compile success (1.0) + correct@1 first-attempt full pass on all 3 remapped operations including unseen operand pairs and negative-number generalization => near-ceiling; no evidence of falling back to familiar lexical meaning of add/sub/mul at any point

methodology_notes: Condition scores computed per llm_learnability.md section 10.6 fixed weights (compile/parse success, Correct@1, test pass rate, specification compliance, unseen-case generalization dominating the observed evidence; repair metrics not exercised since zero repair turns were needed in either trial).

held_out_rule_composition_trials_per_language=1 and prior_conflict_resistance_trials_per_language=1 per primary.json; single predeclared trial per condition was executed for Kotlin as frozen before observing results.

Held-out combinations for I5 were fixed before trial_start: the prompt demonstrates Rule A, Rule B, Rule C only in isolation (never in any pairwise or triple combination as source code), with the sole exception of one narrated arithmetic trace for the composition on the word 'trap' included as a worked reasoning aid to disambiguate rule ordering semantics -- this trace does not provide the Kotlin source or the golden test harness values used for scoring, and 3 of 4 scored test cases (cat, blob, dog) are genuinely unseen combinations.

I6 mapping is a simple 3-way permutation (add<->mul<->sub cyclic swap of real operations) that is reversible in principle (applying the same table again is a well-defined permutation), matching the prior_conflict_resistance methodology requirement of a reversible counterfactual mapping; no semantic traps altering real computable results were used beyond the operation substitution itself.
